question: Does a Cav3-class blocker of known potency reproduce the late-phase reduction of ethosuximide in the Wwox null, and does the effect differ by genotype?
design: One acute PTZ experiment in littermates, same day, concurrent PTZ-alone control in every genotype, pre-specified late-phase window (second half of the hour, where the Fig 7b separation lies) and pre-specified early window; drug-by-genotype interaction in the model; litter and sex as blocks; scorer blind to genotype and drug; terminal brain and plasma exposure of each compound measured in the same animals
arms: Wwox -/- and +/+ (and +/- if litters allow) x {vehicle, ethosuximide as in Cheng, Z944 at an exposure chosen from X0 and measured, optional unrelated-mechanism antiseizure reference} (dose and schedule to be fixed by the executing laboratory; none is recommended here)
readouts: Racine stage per minute (as Fig 7b) plus time to first generalised event; separately: sedation or motor impairment (righting reflex, locomotion), survival to the end of the test, body weight; EEG if available (not a requirement)
controls_and_guards: Concurrent same-day controls (the two null PTZ-alone cohorts of Fig 7b and 7d differ in shape); a wild-type PTZ dose high enough to leave room below the ceiling and above the floor, stated before unblinding; exposure measured, not assumed; seizure suppression, sedation, viability, development and network function reported as separate columns, never one score
decision_rule_fixed_in_advance: (i) Both compounds reduce the late phase in the null and the interaction is supported: consistent with a Cav3-class contribution or a shared benefit, still isoform-blind; (ii) ethosuximide reduces and Z944 does not at measured exposure at or above its Cav3 range: points to a non-Cav3 route for ethosuximide or to pharmacology that does not match; (iii) both reduce in all genotypes: a benefit shared across genotypes (can still matter in WOREE, answers question A not C); (iv) neither reduces: Fig 7b not reproduced
cannot_show: a benefit is not an isoform; no spontaneous-seizure, EEG, development or myelin conclusion; sedation can mimic a lower stage
